svg.title: Kart movement networking plan v2
svg.desc: Updated networking plan for kart movement covering clock sync, per-frame loop, reconciliation with re-simulation, and visual smoothing

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does the client send a ping to measure RTT?')
sendPrompt('What does the server include in the PongPacket?')
sendPrompt('How does the client calculate its starting tick offset?')
sendPrompt('What fields go in an InputPacket?')
sendPrompt('What data does each ring buffer entry store?')
sendPrompt('How does client-side prediction work for the kart?')
sendPrompt('How are input packets sent to the server?')
sendPrompt('How does the server store incoming inputs per client?')
sendPrompt('What tick does the server simulate and why?')
sendPrompt('What is included in a StateSnapshot?')
g.text: tick + pos + vel + rot per kart

svg.text: 3. On snapshot received — re-simulation and correction

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How do we discard stale snapshots?')
sendPrompt('How do we look up the predicted state at the snapshot tick?')
g.text: our predicted state at that tick

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How do we check if the error is large enough to correct?')
sendPrompt('How do we re-simulate forward from snapshot tick to now?')
sendPrompt('How do we apply the physics state correction instantly?')
g.text: pos, vel, rot — instant, no lerp

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Why do we split physics state and visual node?')
sendPrompt('How does the visual node lerp toward the physics state each frame?')
sendPrompt('What is the result of separating physics and visual state?')
sendPrompt('How do we interpolate remote karts smoothly?')

svg.text: repeat ping/pong, nudge tick ±1 — never hard-set during gameplay
simulate_one_frame() must be pure — same inputs always produce same outputs
